title: Hosted API demo — Chat & text generation basics
meeting_summary: AE + SE from Redwood walked Summit Digital through the Hosted API chat/text generation basics: streaming, generation params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retry semantics and idempotency keys, and a short Console/SDK demo. Customer asked security questions (SOC2, SSO, data retention) and raised perf vs cost tradeoffs; they are interested in a short pilot to run 1M tokens/month and requested pricing, security docs, and a benchmark run. Next steps agreed: send pricing + SOC2 report, schedule a 2-hour POC scoping call with infra team next week, and share a sample SDK snippet and retry guidance.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Recording: https://redwood.example/rec/ff-20260304-0197 (auto)
Attendees: Ariel Gomez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jamie Lee (CTO - Summit Digital), Morgan Price (Sr ML Eng), Taylor Kim (Product)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API intro + streaming demo, talk through params and retry behavior; security questions on SOC2 and retention; agreed next steps for pricing and POC scoping.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ariel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ariel from Redwood, and with me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jamie: Hey thanks, Ariel. All good here. Excited to see what you have.
[00:10] Taylor: Yeah thanks, quick heads up we only have about 40 minutes, so demo + Q&A please.
[00:16] Ariel: Totally. We'll keep it focused. Quick agenda: hosted API quick overview, streaming demo for chat generation, go over common parameters (temp, top_p, max_tokens), retry semantics and idempotency, and then console/SDK quick peek.
[00:27] Samir: I'll take the demo and run through a couple of live examples. Note: we'll also point out where Redwood Optimize recommends batching or quantization for cost.
[00:33] Morgan: Great — our primary goal is building a chat assistant embedded in our product, need sub-second-ish latency for short queries and predictable cost at scale.
[00:40] Ariel: Good callout. Can you share current stack quickly? Is this all in-cloud, and what infra?
[00:44] Jamie: We're mostly AWS, ECS for services, infra team uses EKS for some things. No on-prem at this stage.
[00:50] Morgan: We run a custom ranking model and plan to call an LLM for generative responses plus some reranking. We're trying to figure out hosted vs dedicated.
[00:56] Ariel: Perfect — hosted API is usually fastest to get started, predictable per-token billing. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower unit cost — tradeoffs.
[01:05] Taylor: What's the easiest path to test latency? Do you let us run benchmarks?
[01:09] Samir: Yes, we can run benchmark scripts. We also provide a small test harness to exercise typical seq lengths. For hosted, you get regional endpoints and you can pin models.
[01:18] Ariel: Okay Samir, demo?
[01:20] Samir: Yep. Sharing screen — sorry if the deck is fuzzy. First, streaming: we send a streaming response back via chunked HTTP or WebSocket; that means you can render tokens as they arrive.
[01:30] Samir: Example: send /v1/chat/completions with messages array, and set stream=true. We'll start sending delta tokens. Here's a sample curl and a Node snippet — (reads) curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -d '{"model":"redwood-beta-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize our Q1 roadmap"}],"stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
[01:53] Morgan: Sorry, can you repeat the path? Was that /v1/chat/completions?
[01:56] Samir: Yeah, /v1/chat/completions — same pattern as many APIs. Note: products names in the docs sometimes show Redwood API or Redwood Console, sometimes we accidentally refer to Redwood-serve in internal notes, so docs spellings vary.
[02:07] Jamie: Ha, understood. On retries: if a chunk fails mid-stream, what does the client see?
[02:12] Samir: Good question. For streaming, if the connection drops you typically receive a partial output; we recommend using idempotency keys on the request and retrying as a non-streaming request to re-generate full response, or resuming using a cache key for prefix. Our SDKs handle basic retry/backoff automatically — but for at-least-once semantics you should dedupe on your side.
[02:29] Taylor: So idempotency key is an optional header?
[02:31] Samir: Yep; X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key or similar. If you replay with same key and the request completed previously, you'll get the same result (or a stored response) depending on the model variant.
[02:40] Morgan: And recommended backoff? Exponential jitter?
[02:42] Samir: We recommend exponential backoff with full jitter, start at 200ms, cap at 10s, and retry up to 3 times for transient 5xx errors. For rate-limited 429s, honor Retry-After header. We'll send best-practice snippets after.
[02:55] Ariel: Let's switch to generation params. Samir, quick primer.
[02:58] Samir: Sure. Temperature controls randomness (0 to 2 typical). Top_p does nucleus sampling. Max_tokens controls output length; also set stop sequences if you need structured output. Another important one is top_k in some models. For deterministic outputs set temp=0 and top_p=1.
[03:14] Morgan: Do you expose logprobs or token-level metadata?
[03:18] Samir: Yes, you can request token metadata in the API — but be aware of extra cost. Also, streaming doesn't include full logprob arrays by default.
[03:26] Taylor: Any guidance on batching to save cost?
[03:29] Samir: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching thresholds. For hosted API, our runtime supports continuous batching: if you send many small requests, it will batch them in the backend transparently but you can tune batching in the console. There's also prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[03:44] Jamie: What's the SLA/uptime for hosted?
[03:46] Ariel: Hosted has a baseline SLA, and Dedicated can get higher SLA and reserved throughput. We'll attach exact SLA numbers in the pricing doc.
[03:53] Morgan: Security: we need SOC 2, SSO, SAML, audit logs, and encryption at rest with customer KMS.
[03:59] Ariel: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC in Console, audit logs, and KMS integrations for Private deployments; hosted can use Redwood-managed keys but we also support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[04:12] Taylor: What about data retention and deletion? We have compliance requirements to delete conversation data after 30 days unless stored in our systems.
[04:18] Samir: You can configure retention settings in Console and opt out of data retention for hosted in some plans; for PII-sensitive workflows we often recommend Private deployment or dedicated offer. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[04:30] Ariel: Samir, can you run a quick live prompt showing streaming vs non-streaming?
[04:33] Samir: Sure. Typing an example: prompt — "Write a short product blurb for Summit Digital's chat assistant". Sending with stream=true.
[04:42] [stream events begin, client renders tokens]
[04:45] Samir: You can see tokens arrive progressively; that gives perceived latency improvement. If you need token-level highlighting, you can render partial tokens.
[04:52] Taylor: Looks good. If we need structured output (JSON), do you suggest function-calling or forcing a JSON schema?
[04:57] Samir: We support both. Function/tool calling helps keep outputs consistent and can reduce parsing errors. You can also use a strict schema and stop sequences. For many customers, function calling plus validation is the sweet spot.
[05:10] Morgan: On cost predictability: if we stream or use longer max_tokens, do you meter differently?
[05:14] Ariel: Billing is per token generated + input tokens. Streaming doesn't change metering; it's just a delivery mode. Optimize helps recommend shorter max_tokens and caching to lower costs.
[05:23] Jamie: How about rate limits? We may have spikes.
[05:26] Samir: There's per-account rate limiting and per-route quotas. For higher throughput you can request increases or move to Dedicated. Also, continuous batching reduces RPCs.
[05:36] Taylor: Any notes about model variants? We may want cheaper variants for lower criticality flows.
[05:40] Samir: Yes we have model catalog with verified performance profiles; Redwood can route to cheaper quantized variants when you set routing policy for cost-first. That routing is configurable in the Console.
[05:52] Morgan: Will model switching affect output consistency? We need deterministic behavior for certain flows.
[05:57] Samir: There will be differences — we recommend canary rollouts and A/B tests via Console rollouts to measure regressions. Optimize can run evals on your prompt sets.
[06:08] Ariel: Quick aside — do you have internal benchmarks we can share?
[06:11] Jamie: Sorry, Ariel I meant do you run a benchmark against our prompts?
[06:14] Samir: Yes we can run a benchmark with your sample prompts — typically takes a day to run at scale; we'll propose a small benchmark as part of the POC.
[06:23] Taylor: Ok let's talk pilot sizing — we mentioned ~1M tokens/month in the intake form. Is that enough to estimate cost?
[06:29] Ariel: Yes that's a good starting point. We'll model a few traffic patterns: bursty (spikes) vs steady. For hosted, see pricing tiers; we'll send a sample cost model.
[06:38] Morgan: Any enterprise legal requirements — do you do data processing agreements?
[06:41] Ariel: Yes we have DPA and standard security addenda. For Private we do on-prem contracts.
[06:47] Taylor: Can you show the Console real quick?
[06:49] Samir: Switching screens — Console home, model catalog, routes, and Optimize suggestions. Here you can see per-route latency and token cost, plus per-token breakdown and traces. (screen note: some labels read "Redwood-Console" vs "Redwood Console" inconsistently).
[07:05] Samir: In Optimize tab you can see batch size suggestions and a recommended quantization profile for each model. You can also pin a model version and set rollout policies.
[07:13] Jamie: Nice. For PII flows we want audit logs exported to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[07:18] Samir: Yes, audit logs can stream to S3 or to your SIEM via a connector; retention settings are configurable.
[07:24] Morgan: Any limits on embedding use? We plan to use embeddings for semantic search too.
[07:28] Ariel: Embeddings endpoints are separate metering; you can use hosted embeddings or Dedicated. Optimize has recommendations for embeddings dimensionality vs cost.
[07:36] Taylor: Let's move to objections — our infra team worries about vendor lock-in. What do you recommend?
[07:41] Ariel: We recommend keeping prompts and evaluation harness in your repo, using vendor-agnostic API layers (we keep standard REST shape), and using our export tools to snapshot model versions. Also you can run Private for more portability.
[07:55] Jamie: Any hard limits on token size? We have some long context windows (8k+).
[07:59] Samir: We support multiple sequence length profiles; some model variants handle 32k. We'll map which model fits your context windows in the POC scoping.
[08:07] Taylor: Ok, action items recap?
[08:09] Ariel: Yes: I'll send pricing + SLA + SOC2 summary by Friday; Samir will send SDK and retry examples by Thursday; Samir will also propose a benchmark plan and scoping agenda. Jamie/Taylor to provide POC attendee list and infra contact.
[08:22] Jamie: Sounds good. One more quick question — for streaming, is there a maximum time to keep an open stream?
[08:27] Samir: Streams are subject to connection timeouts — we recommend 60s for most UI flows; longer-running generations should use non-streaming or chunked resumable approaches. We'll add details in the guide.
[08:38] Taylor: Awesome. Thanks, this was helpful and concise.
[08:40] Ariel: Great. We'll follow up with the docs and we'll schedule a POC scoping next week. Thanks everyone.
[08:47] Meeting end.
